text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock climbed 2.3% today as crude oil prices surged toward $100 a barrel, driven by escalating U.S.-Iran tensions in the Middle East. Brent crude — the global oil benchmark — reached nearly $100, while U.S. crude hit $99, stoking concerns about potential supply disruptions. For a refiner like Marathon, higher oil prices typically support margins when refineries can pass costs through to fuel sales, and the company is operating at 98% capacity, positioned to benefit from the tightening energy market.

The stock's broader 9.7% rally over two weeks reflects this geopolitical tailwind: each new round of U.S.-Iran strikes has pushed oil higher and fueled demand expectations, lifting refiners along with the commodity. With global oil supplies now at risk and storage levels relatively low (gasoline and diesel inventories are modest), the refining sector is riding a wave of supply-side fear that keeps crude prices elevated.
